triggers.grounds: EXCL lane, count object named then swept. The flagged sentence writes 'any claim of a construction unique to this seam' with no adjacent digit-bearing sweep citation. Re-swept: the object is the whole proverb-line of oshb:Prov.14.12, and a contiguous skeleton sweep of that line returns 2 verses (Prov.14.12, Prov.16.25); a direct byte comparison of the two full pointed verses is equal, so the row's 'recurs verbatim at Prov.16.25 (byte tier)' is byte-TRUE at the tier it names. The hinge-word object is a DIFFERENT set: a contiguous skeleton sweep of וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ returns 5 verses (Prov.5.4, Prov.14.12, Prov.14.13, Prov.16.25, Prov.20.21), of which only 14:12 and 14:13 are adjacent. The universal claim is therefore true but ships without its digit, so under the EXCL lane test this is a confirmed_defect at low severity (disclosure), not an evidence defect.

findings.claim: The uniqueness disclosure in strongest_rejected_alternative carries no adjacent digit-bearing sweep citation naming its count object.
findings.grounds: Strategy S8 requires every universal claim to carry an adjacent digit that names the swept object and unit. Both available digits are absent from the field: the full-line object sweeps to 2 verses (Prov.14.12, Prov.16.25; contiguous skeleton) and the hinge-word object וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ sweeps to 5 verses (Prov.5.4, Prov.14.12, Prov.14.13, Prov.16.25, Prov.20.21; contiguous skeleton). Both underlying facts are byte-true; only the digits are missing.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to strongest_rejected_alternative only: append the digit with its object, e.g. '(the whole line recurs in 2 verses book-wide, contiguous skeleton sweep: Prov.14.12, Prov.16.25)'.

findings.claim: The cluster's forward seam carries an undisclosed straddling catchword exactly as heavy as the row's own internal glue, and the row nonetheless ships at medium with no frontier posture, against the book's own sub-two-token rule.
findings.grounds: Skeleton content-token overlap computed from consonantal_index.json. Prov.14.12 and Prov.14.13 share exactly ONE token (וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ, byte at oshb:Prov.14.13; the 14:12 form וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ is byte at oshb:Prov.14.12) and that single token is the row's entire lexical glue. Prov.14.13 and Prov.14.14 ALSO share exactly ONE token (לֵ֑ב at oshb:Prov.14.13 against לֵ֑ב at oshb:Prov.14.14), so the row's forward seam is straddled by a catchword of equal count, disclosed by neither this row nor the Prov.14.14 row. The backward seam adds a root-level straddle (יְשָׁרִ֣ים at oshb:Prov.14.11 against יָ֭שָׁר at oshb:Prov.14.12 - one lexeme, two skeleton tokens). The standing cross-seam rule makes a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam an argument for continuity unless disclosed, and strategy S7 places catchword-cluster rows whose cohesion is thinner than two shared content tokens in the expected-low-confidence class; this row ships confidence medium with frontier_flag_considered false. In the pairing's favour, and verifiable: the shared form opens the B-colon in BOTH verses, standing immediately after the atnach (אִ֑ישׁ in 14:12, לֵ֑ב in 14:13), so the catchword is slot-parallel rather than incidental - but the two-shared-root test that the Prov.16.18-16.19 cluster passes is not met here.
findings.proposed_change: No respan proposed. Field repair plus calibration: disclose the straddling catchword at the 14:13|14:14 seam and weigh it (a SEAM-PAIR cure, one edit shared with the Prov.14.14 row, which omits the same disclosure), and either re-band confidence to medium_low with the frontier posture S7 anticipates for sub-two-token catchword clusters, or add a second byte-grounded shared content token as a ground.

findings.claim: The phrase 'the identical appearance-vs-outcome template' applies a tier-grade identity word to a structural analogy, with no byte object and no digit.
findings.grounds: check_universals flags this claim in boundary_rationale as an identical/verbatim-class universal with no sweep digit in its sentence. The two A-cola are not structurally identical on the bytes: oshb:Prov.14.12 opens on an appearance-versus-reality assertion (יֵ֤שׁ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יָ֭שָׁר לִפְנֵי אִ֑ישׁ) while oshb:Prov.14.13 opens on a concurrent real state (גַּם בִּשְׂח֥וֹק יִכְאַב לֵ֑ב) - the first says a way SEEMS right, the second says the heart DOES ache. Strategy S6 also bars a shared theme from serving as a cluster's glue, so this second ground cannot carry the weight the field assigns it as 'a second, independently named ground'.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale: replace 'identical' with a non-tier word such as 'parallel' or 'shared', or supply the byte object the identity claim is measured against.

triggers.grounds: LOWBAND calibration. The stated reason for the band is honest and byte-checkable: the A-colon subject is the compound ס֣וּג לֵ֑ב (byte at oshb:Prov.14.14), a genuine lexical crux, and the ellipsis is real - the B-colon וּ֝מֵעָלָ֗יו אִ֣ישׁ טֽוֹב carries no verb, so the A-colon verb יִ֭שְׂבַּע must be supplied. Strategy S7 places lexical cruxes in the expected-low-confidence class and requires bespoke uncertainty text; this row's text is row-specific rather than boilerplate, and frontier_flag_considered is true. The seam is sound at that band: the C2 atomic default governs, the forward seam Prov.14.14|Prov.14.15 shares 0 skeleton content tokens, and pmarks_Prov.json records no parashah, paseq or K/Q entry at Prov.14.14 for the row to have missed. The band is neither over-stated nor masking a byte-defective warrant, so the trigger itself is not a defect; the byte-false comparison claim in this row is recorded separately as a finding.

findings.claim: The disclaimer that the verse 'shares no lexeme' with Prov.13.1-13.2 is byte-false: it shares two lexemes with Prov.13.2.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale asserts the verse 'is not adjacent to those and shares no lexeme with them'. Skeleton content-token comparison from consonantal_index.json: Prov.14.14 and Prov.13.2 share TWO tokens. oshb:Prov.13.2 carries אִ֭ישׁ and ט֑וֹב; oshb:Prov.14.14 carries אִ֣ישׁ and טֽוֹב - the same two lexemes, differing only in accents. Prov.13.1 does share nothing with Prov.14.14, so the claim is false for one of the two verses it names, not both. It is a no-class universal shipped without a digit, and check_universals does not carry this phrasing in its lexicon, so it passed Tier-0 unflagged. It is not load-bearing - the boundary rests on the in-verse ellipsis and the rejected alternative rests on the compound noun's gloss being unnecessary - hence medium, not high.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale: strike the disclaimer, or correct it to name the two shared lexemes and state that the shared vocabulary is generic and non-adjacent, so the comparison is not a cohesion claim.

findings.claim: The backward seam Prov.14.13|Prov.14.14 is straddled by a shared content token that this row does not disclose.
findings.grounds: oshb:Prov.14.13 carries לֵ֑ב and oshb:Prov.14.14 carries לֵ֑ב - one shared skeleton content token across the row's own backward seam (consonantal_index.json overlap). The standing cross-seam rule makes such a straddle an argument for continuity unless disclosed, and neither this row nor the Prov.14.12-14.13 row discloses it. Low rather than medium because this is a default-atomic C2 row, so the token does not have to defeat a cluster warrant here; the same omission on the cluster side of the seam is recorded at medium.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: disclose the straddling token at the backward seam and weigh it as too generic to draw the boundary backward. Seam-pair cure - ONE edit shared with the Prov.14.12-14.13 row.

triggers.grounds: LOWBAND calibration; the row is well-calibrated and its grounds are byte-sound. The central observation is byte-true: the B-colon of oshb:Prov.14.33 is וּבְקֶ֥רֶב כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים תִּוָּדֵֽעַ and carries no negative particle, and the second witness agrees - web:Prov.14.33 renders wisdom as being made known even in the inward part of fools - so the row reports the staged bytes accurately at both witnesses. Its refusal to supply a negator is exactly what strategy S4 requires: comparative-tradition material is metadata in Prov and can be neither boundary evidence nor a text-critical warrant here, and the row rejects the conjecture on that ground rather than importing it. The seam is sound at any band under the C2 atomic default: Prov.14.32 and Prov.14.33 share 0 skeleton content tokens and Prov.14.33 and Prov.14.34 share 0, so nothing straddles either edge to be disclosed. pmarks_Prov.json records no parashah, paseq, K/Q or special-letter entry at Prov.14.33 and the row claims none; the book's one x-small seg is at Prov.16.28 and is untouched. The low band is honestly reasoned (an unresolved in-verse crux, not a boundary doubt), frontier_flag_considered is true, and the uncertainty text is bespoke as S7 requires. No tier-4 fact does any work anywhere in the row: no punctuation, paragraphing, heading or verse-division claim appears.

LOWBAND calibration; well-calibrated with byte-sound grounds. The driver splice וְחֶ֖סֶד collates BYTE at oshb:Prov.14.34, the tier the field names. The homograph disclosure is Prov-internally consistent: a contiguous skeleton sweep of the noun returns 11 verses (Prov.3.3, 11.17, 14.22, 14.34, 16.6, 19.22, 20.6, 20.28, 21.21, 25.10, 31.26), all one spelling, so the two senses genuinely are not spellable apart and the row's 'without a distinguishing point' is not an idle claim. The rival is rejected on the SECOND WITNESS's rendering at web:Prov.14.34, which pairs the noun with sin as a disgrace - a translation's lexical choice, which the toolkit expressly admits as argument alongside the pointed bytes, and NOT tier-4 metadata: no punctuation, paragraph, poetry-line, heading, footnote or verse-division fact is used anywhere in the row. The seam is sound: Prov.14.33|Prov.14.34 and Prov.14.34|Prov.14.35 each share 0 skeleton content tokens, so the C2 atomic default holds with nothing straddling either edge. pmarks_Prov.json records no mark of any class at Prov.14.34 and the row claims none. Strategy S7 names the homograph zone as an expected low-confidence region; medium_low with frontier_flag_considered true and bespoke crux text is exactly that posture, and the ambiguity is disclosed rather than silently resolved.

LOWBAND calibration; the band is honest and the evidence behind it is byte-sound. The K/Q ground is inventory-true and correctly tiered: pmarks_Prov.json kq carries exactly 1 note at Prov.15.14, the inventory value is a bare count (which the row correctly labels count-only), and the row derives the identification from the verse bytes rather than from the inventory - the inline unpointed ופני and the pointed וּפִ֥י BOTH collate byte at oshb:Prov.15.14, so the inline-ketiv reading is byte-visible, not asserted. The near-duplicate ground is byte-true: oshb:Prov.15.2 and oshb:Prov.15.14 share 4 skeleton content tokens, their closing cola differing only in the verb (יַבִּ֥יעַ against יִרְעֶ֥ה), so 'almost word for word' is accurate; and 15:14 minus 15:2 is 12, so 'twelve lines apart' is arithmetically right. Both seams are disclosed and correctly weighed - the shared heart token really does straddle both edges (skeleton overlap Prov.15.13|Prov.15.14 and Prov.15.14|Prov.15.15, one token each) and the row names it and rejects it as too generic, which is the cross-seam rule performed rather than skipped. Strategy S7 names K/Q verses as an expected low-confidence region; medium_low with frontier_flag_considered true and bespoke text is that posture. The two defects recorded below are a tier-disclosure shortfall and register; neither touches the band.

findings.claim: One pointed splice is cited at two refs but stands at only one of them at byte tier, with no tier named for the other.
findings.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative writes the heart token as לֵ֣ב and cites it as recurring 'at both the backward seam (oshb:Prov.15.13) and the forward seam (oshb:Prov.15.15)'. Collated at each cited ref with collate.py: byte at oshb:Prov.15.13 and byte at the row's own oshb:Prov.15.14, but ACCENT_STRIPPED at oshb:Prov.15.15, where the form standing in the verse is לֵ֝֗ב. The toolkit rules only the byte tier quotation-grade for pointed text and requires accent_stripped and skeleton citations to be labelled as such in prose; no tier is named here. The substance is true - the token does recur at both neighbours - so this is a citation/disclosure shortfall, not a false claim.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to strongest_rejected_alternative: either name the tier for the forward-seam arm, or splice the 15:15 form separately so each cited ref carries the form that actually stands in it (the Prov.15.15 row already uses that second form, so both are in the corpus).

findings.claim: Row prose carries staging-inventory and toolkit-catalog names, and quotes WEB wording outside the mandated quote convention.
findings.grounds: REGISTER LAW test 1 (cosmetic; no argumentative claim about another row): observed_substrate_signals writes '(pmarks: 1 note, count-only)' and '(INLINE-KETIV HAZARD at oshb:Prov.15.14)' - a staging inventory name and a toolkit hazard-catalog label inside prose that must describe the text, not the apparatus. The inventory was used CORRECTLY (pmarks_Prov.json kq at Prov.15.14 = 1), so this is register, not evidence. Separately, device_notes quotes WEB wording of web:Prov.15.2 in straight single quotes with a bare ref, where the book-wide convention requires curly double quotes plus an inline web: ref in the same field; because straight quotes were used, check_web_quotes saw 0 quotes in the row and returned GREEN, so the run went unverified by Tier-0.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: restate the K/Q disclosure without the inventory and hazard-catalog names (e.g. 'one ketiv/qere note stands at Prov.15.14, count-only in the single witness'), and re-set the WEB fragment in curly double quotes with an inline web:Prov.15.2 in the same field.

triggers.grounds: EXCL lane, count object named then swept. The flagged sentence says the two verses 'have no other point of lexical contact' with no adjacent digit-bearing citation. Re-swept with the object named as skeleton content tokens (consonantal_index.json): oshb:Prov.15.25 and oshb:Prov.15.26 share EXACTLY ONE token - יְהוָ֑ה in 15:25 against יְ֭הוָה in 15:26 - and zero others at token or lexeme level. The claim is therefore byte-TRUE and simply ships without its digit, so under the EXCL lane test this is a confirmed_defect at low severity (disclosure). Verified sound alongside it, and NOT defects: the paseq disclosure is inventory-true (pmarks_Prov.json paseq at Prov.15.25 = 1 seg), is labelled single-witness and explicitly corroborating rather than a driver, and asserts no intra-verse position, so check_marks raised no paseq_position_warn against the count-only inventory; the backward seam Prov.15.24|Prov.15.25 shares 0 skeleton content tokens; and the antithesis the row argues is byte-real (יִסַּ֥ח against וְ֝יַצֵּ֗ב at oshb:Prov.15.25).

findings.claim: The exclusivity ground in strongest_rejected_alternative carries no adjacent digit-bearing sweep citation naming its count object.
findings.grounds: Strategy S8 requires an adjacent digit naming the swept object and unit on every universal claim. The digit exists and is favourable to the row: the shared skeleton content-token set across Prov.15.25 and Prov.15.26 is exactly one token, with 0 further shared tokens, so the rejection ground is true and merely undocumented. citation_sweep and check_marks both returned clean on this row; the shortfall is the missing digit alone.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to strongest_rejected_alternative: name the object and the digit, e.g. 'the shared set is one token (the divine name); 0 further content tokens are shared across the seam'.

triggers.grounds: LOWBAND calibration; the band is honest and the cluster's cohesion is byte-real. Every splice collates BYTE at its cited ref: רֽוּחַ at oshb:Prov.16.18 and ר֭וּחַ at oshb:Prov.16.19 (one skeleton token, in parallel construct slots); גָּא֑וֹן at oshb:Prov.16.18 and גֵּאִֽים at oshb:Prov.16.19 (two distinct attested spellings of one root - so the row's 'two shared roots' names ROOTS, not tokens, and is count-object-correct: the exact-token overlap of the two verses is 1). The K/Q ground is inventory-true: pmarks_Prov.json kq at Prov.16.19 = 1 note, and the inline unpointed עניים and the pointed עֲנָוִ֑ים both collate byte at oshb:Prov.16.19, so the ketiv/qere is byte-visible. Seams: Prov.16.17|Prov.16.18 shares 0 skeleton content tokens; the forward seam's shared token (ט֣וֹב against ט֑וֹב) is disclosed and rejected at the seam by the Prov.16.20 row, and both neighbour rows argue this seam compatibly with this one, so cross-row coherence holds. Strategy S7 places K/Q cruxes in the expected-low-confidence class, which is precisely the reason the row states for its band; two shared roots in consecutive verses is a stronger cluster warrant than S6 requires, so the band is conservative rather than over-stated. NOTE for the record: check_marks raised two kq_claim flags at Prov.16.18 on this row and both are window artifacts, not defects - the tool appends boundary_evidence_refs to the prose, and the plus-or-minus-120-character window around the device_notes K/Q mention (whose ref is written in colon form, which the tool's dotted pattern does not match) reaches only as far as the first refs entry, web:Prov.16.18. Every K/Q claim in the row is anchored to Prov.16.19, which the inventory confirms.

findings.claim: Two driver splices are cut one word shorter than the glosses attached to them.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale glosses רֽוּחַ as 'height of spirit' and ר֭וּחַ as 'lowly of spirit', but each splice is the single noun while each gloss renders the two-word construct phrase; gloss extent must equal splice extent. The full phrases exist and are quotation-grade: גֹּ֣בַהּ רֽוּחַ collates BYTE at oshb:Prov.16.18 and שְׁפַל ר֭וּחַ collates BYTE at oshb:Prov.16.19, and the Prov.16.20 row already cites both in that fuller form. The substantive claim - one shared noun standing in parallel construct slots - is true either way, so this is mechanical.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale: extend each splice to the two-word construct phrase, or re-cut each gloss to the single noun.

findings.claim: Two digit-bearing citations name a count without naming the swept domain, and are byte-false if read book-wide.
findings.grounds: observed_substrate_signals writes '(sweep: 2 consecutive verses)' twice. Read as pair-scoped the digits are true; read as book-wide sweep digits - which is how a citation labelled 'sweep' reads under SEMANTIC-CLASS COUNT DISCIPLINE, where the object is named FIRST and then counted - both are byte-false. Book-wide contiguous skeleton sweeps: the shared noun returns 20 verses (Prov.1.23, 11.13, 11.29, 14.29, 15.4, 15.13, 16.2, 16.18, 16.19, 16.32, 17.22, 17.27, 18.14, 25.14, 25.23, 25.28, 27.16, 29.11, 29.23, 30.4), and the two pride-root spellings return 2 verses each (גָּא֑וֹן at Prov.8.13 and Prov.16.18; גֵּאִֽים at Prov.15.25 and Prov.16.19). check_universals does not flag a parenthetical that already carries a digit, so this passed Tier-0.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to observed_substrate_signals: give each digit its domain, e.g. '2 of the 20 book-wide verses carrying this noun, and the only consecutive pair' and '2 verses per attested spelling book-wide, adjacent only here'.

findings.claim: device_notes compares this row's confidence field to another row's, which is process description rather than text description.
findings.grounds: REGISTER LAW test 1: 'the ketiv/qere crux at 16:19 is the reason this cluster's confidence sits lower than the 16:12-16:15 run' names a row FIELD (confidence) and ranks it against another row's value. The verse anchoring is correct, so this is not an unanchored cross-row reference, and the sentence carries no byte assertion to re-derive under test 2 - but confidence is apparatus, not text, and its comparative value is unverifiable from this row's own bytes. Purely cosmetic, hence low.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to device_notes: state the crux and its effect on the reading without the cross-row confidence comparison.

triggers.grounds: EXCL lane, count object named then swept. boundary_rationale says the verse's two maxims are 'bound only by a shared theme of scorn rather than a repeated word', with no adjacent digit. Re-swept with the object named as skeleton content tokens shared BETWEEN THE TWO COLA of oshb:Prov.17.5 - A-colon לֹעֵ֣ג לָ֭רָשׁ חֵרֵ֣ף עֹשֵׂ֑הוּ against B-colon שָׂמֵ֥חַ לְ֝אֵ֗יד לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶֽה - the count is 0. The same shortfall recurs in strongest_rejected_alternative ('no token repeats across either seam'), which is likewise byte-true: Prov.17.4 and Prov.17.5 share 0 skeleton content tokens and Prov.17.5 and Prov.17.6 share 0. findings.claim: Two universal claims, one in each driver field, ship without an adjacent digit-bearing sweep citation naming the count object.
findings.grounds: Strategy S8 requires the digit on every only-class or no-class claim. Both digits are 0 and both favour the row: 0 skeleton content tokens shared between the two cola of oshb:Prov.17.5, and 0 shared across each seam (Prov.17.4|Prov.17.5 and Prov.17.5|Prov.17.6). check_universals did not flag either sentence, so the shortfall passed Tier-0.

findings.claim: Two verses argued outside the row's span are absent from boundary_evidence_refs, and the malformed ref form used for them hides the gap from the Tier-0 gate.
findings.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative argues Prov.17.4 and Prov.17.6, both outside the span Prov.17.5-Prov.17.5, but boundary_evidence_refs carries only web:Prov.17.5. Both neighbour rows mirror what they argue (the Prov.17.4 row lists web:Prov.17.3 and web:Prov.17.5; the Prov.17.6 row lists web:Prov.17.5 and web:Prov.17.7), so this row is the outlier within its own seam-neighbourhood. The mentions are written in a book-less dotted form that matches neither check_refs_mirror's Prov.C.V pattern nor its bare colon pattern, which is why the tool returns GREEN on this row: the mirror gap is real but invisible to Tier-0. The underlying rejection claim is byte-true (0 shared tokens across either seam), so this is mechanical, not an evidence defect.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: add web:Prov.17.4 and web:Prov.17.6 to boundary_evidence_refs, and rewrite the prose mentions in the book's colon form so the Tier-0 mirror gate can see them.
